description:
HushTumblr v0.0.11: 57 patches for Tumblr 47.0.0.108, which needs Android 8 or newer. Two new switches, Hide reblogs of your posts and Tags open the blog's tag search. Hide ads catches the app promos on tag pages, Blaze buttons come off posts, and settings work better with a keyboard or TalkBack. Validation: 1331 runtime tests passed. All 321 patch tests passed. All 57 patches applied without forcing to Tumblr 47.0.0.108. Needs Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer. The .mpp is a patch bundle, not a Tumblr APK. Uninstall the stock app first, then sign in with your email and a Tumblr password.

### What's new

* Line between posts only draws between two posts now. It used to show up under headings like "Looking for more?", above carousels and around buttons too, where it didn't divide anything. Sponsored and Blaze posts still count as posts.
* Hide ads now takes out the one-line app promos that tag pages and search results slip between posts, like "Made with WordPress" with its Install button.
* Dark background color now reaches the row of buttons under your own posts too, the one with Blaze, delete and edit. It kept a lighter gray strip with a rounded bottom under each post, which stood out on a black background. It takes the card's color now on your blog, in drafts, the queue and scheduled posts. With the switch off or HushTumblr paused it's Tumblr's gray as before.
* Hide Blaze prompts now takes the Blaze buttons off posts too. The flame under your own posts goes, and so does Blaze in a post's three-dot menu, Blaze in the share sheet and Promote in a community post's menu. Delete and edit keep their places. Your Blaze dashboard and the Keep Blaze posts switch under Hide ads work as before, and with the switch off or HushTumblr paused every button is back.
* Reveal allowed mature content now opens labeled posts on the first screen after Tumblr starts. Tumblr picks each post's cover while it lays out the dashboard, and that usually happened before its answer about your Content Labels setting came back, so the first posts kept their cover until a refresh. HushTumblr now keeps the last yes for your account for up to a day and checks again in the background every time. A no, or an answer it can't read, wipes it at once. The diagnostic report also counts the checks, the answers and the covers lifted, so a cover that stays up shows where it stopped.
* New **Tags open the blog's tag search** switch on the Posts page, off by default. Tapping a tag under a post opens that blog's own search for the tag, the page you'd see at blog.tumblr.com/tagged, instead of a search of all of Tumblr. It works in the dashboard, other feeds and a post you open by itself. A post with no blog name to go on, or a community's post, keeps Tumblr's usual search.
* New **Hide reblogs of your posts** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes other people's reblogs of your posts out of your dashboard, so a post of yours that's going around doesn't keep coming back to you between the posts of people you follow. A reblog counts when it came straight from one of your blogs or when one of your blogs made the original post. Your own reblogs stay unless **Hide your own reblogs** is on too. Your blog, a post you open by itself and the rest of Tumblr still show them all.
* Settings with TalkBack: flipping a switch that needs a restart keeps your place on that switch now. The Restart row showing up above it used to grab the focus and read itself out, and then the switch's "Restart Tumblr to apply" line got read again on its own. A switch also says its state once now, instead of "on, Switch" and then "ON, Switch" a second time.
* Turning Hide ads off with Tumblr open doesn't close Tumblr anymore when a feed reloads before the restart (changing the text size did it). The feed went to load a Smart banner ad, and Hide ads had kept that ad network from being set up when Tumblr started. Whatever Hide ads turned off now stays off until you restart Tumblr, which the restart row already asks for, and Disable analytics works the same way.
* Custom font: picking a font while Tumblr couldn't save its settings used to put the new file in place under the old font's name. Nothing changes now until the new name is saved. Two picks made close together can't mix their files anymore, and a font that couldn't be copied because storage is full isn't called a broken file.
* Settings with TalkBack: a refused save in the word lists is read once now. It was read twice, from a pop-up and again from the line under the field.
* Settings with TalkBack: coming back from the file picker (Choose a font file, Import settings, Export settings) puts you back on the row you opened it from. TalkBack used to start over at the top of the page.
* Arrow keys work on the settings page. With a keyboard or a D-pad they did nothing there until Tab was pressed, since the page itself held on to the focus.
* Settings with a keyboard: going Back to the main settings page leaves your keys on the row you opened, with TalkBack on or off. That holds after the screen was redrawn too, and a row that sat half off the edge comes all the way into view. The next arrow key used to start from a different row.
* Settings with a keyboard: the first arrow key after you've touched the page lands on the top row in view, and the "HushTumblr is on" card stays where it was. That key used to scroll the card away, and TalkBack read nothing for it.
* Settings with a keyboard or D-pad: the card's Pause button isn't a stop for arrow keys anymore. Pressing Enter on it opened Quick setups instead of pausing. TalkBack still reaches and presses it, and the Pause HushTumblr switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page works with keys.
* Settings with a keyboard: pausing from the "HushTumblr is on" card keeps the card where it was, instead of the Restart row pushing it off the top. TalkBack stays on the card's button, which now says Undo. Flipping a switch at the top of a page with keys also shows the Restart row above it now.
* Settings with a keyboard or TalkBack: focus stays where it was while Tab order or a word list saves. It used to jump to the dialog's buttons and read them out before the answer.
* Manage muted posts with TalkBack or a keyboard: a failed mute or unmute is read once, and its notice shows under the list, so the row you were on stays put. Undo also stays while you're on it instead of going away after 10 seconds. With a keyboard or D-pad, trying again after a failed unmute takes one press, not two.
* Settings with a keyboard or D-pad: flipping a switch keeps the selection on that switch. It used to jump to the switch under it, or to the top row of scrolled search results, so the next press flipped the wrong one.

### Behind the scenes

* **Tooling:** The source audit reads Jman's Patch Bundle Registry through its new API and asks again with fewer rows when a page fails. It also reads every page of a GitHub code search now. Before, it stopped at the first page that came back short and missed files.
* **Tooling:** A release checks the source census when it's cut and again before anything goes up on GitHub. A census refreshed after the cut no longer keeps the publish step from running.
